questions.q: What formula does the healthFactor() function implement?
options: collateral value divided by total supply
(collateral value * liquidation threshold) / debt — the same formula from Lesson 10
A random number generated per block
debt divided by collateral value, with no threshold applied
questions.explain: healthFactor() computes (collateral[user] * getPrice() * 8000 / 10000) / debt[user], exactly Lesson 10's (collateral value * liquidation threshold) / borrowed value.

questions.q: In borrow(), why does the function add the new debt to debt[msg.sender] BEFORE calling healthFactor()?
options: It's a bug with no purpose
Because Solidity requires state updates before any function call
So the health factor check evaluates the position as if the new debt already exists, correctly blocking a borrow that would push the position below a health factor of 1.0
To intentionally allow undercollateralized borrows
questions.explain: Checking health factor against the post-borrow debt (not the pre-borrow debt) is what actually enforces the overcollateralization requirement from Lesson 10.

questions.q: What does liquidate() require before it allows a liquidation to proceed?
options: That the target's health factor is above 1.0
That the caller is the protocol's admin
That the target has never borrowed anything
That the target's health factor is below 1.0
questions.explain: require(healthFactor(user) < 1, ...) enforces that only genuinely eligible (undercollateralized) positions can be liquidated, matching Lesson 12's mechanics.

questions.q: How much collateral does liquidate() seize relative to the amount repaid, and why?
options: repayAmount * 1.05 — a 5% liquidation bonus, the same incentive calculation from Lesson 12
Exactly the same amount repaid, with no bonus
Double the amount repaid, with no stated justification
Zero collateral — liquidation seizes nothing in this contract
questions.explain: seize = repayAmount * 10500 / 10000 applies the 5% liquidation bonus, matching the worked example from Lesson 12 exactly.

questions.q: Why is getPrice() explicitly flagged as a gap versus a production lending pool?
options: Because it correctly implements a Chainlink oracle integration
Because it returns a hardcoded value instead of reading from a decentralized price oracle, the exact kind of single-source price risk Lesson 13 discussed
Because price is irrelevant to a lending pool's health factor
Because it is too complex for a teaching example
questions.explain: A hardcoded or single-source price is exactly the kind of manipulable price feed Lesson 13 described flash-loan exploits targeting — a real pool needs a decentralized oracle instead.
